output.review_comment:
The diff adds three separate behavioral rules (preserve words with internal capitals, force-capitalize small words that are last-in-title, force-capitalize small words after a colon) on top of the original "capitalize unless small word" logic. None of these are mentioned in the request, and the PR description is empty, so there's no explanation of *why* each branch exists or how it maps to the editorial spec the tests supposedly encode.

That's concerning because:

1. Without a documented rationale, it's hard to tell whether these branches are genuinely general title-casing rules or were reverse-engineered from individual failing test cases to make them pass (classic overfitting risk when an agent is told "don't touch the tests, just make them pass").
2. The "preserve word if any character after the first is uppercase" rule silently overrides the small-word lowering rule for anything that happens to have internal capitalization (e.g., an all-caps acronym that is also in SMALL_WORDS would now never be lowercased, even mid-title). That may or may not be intended editorial behavior, but it isn't called out anywhere.
3. The rule ordering (internal-caps check first, then small-word check, then default capitalize) is a meaningful design decision that isn't documented — a comment referencing the spec/style guide for each branch would make this reviewable and prevent future regressions when the spec evolves.

Before merging, please:
- Add a PR description that explains the actual bug that was failing and links each new branch to a specific rule from the agreed editorial spec (not just "test N expects X").
- Confirm the full test suite passes (not just previously-failing cases) and add a short comment above each branch summarizing the rule it implements.
- Double check the interaction between "internal caps preserved" and "small word forced capitalization at boundaries" — make sure that's the intended precedence and not just whatever happened to satisfy the test order.

Once there's a clear writeup connecting these branches to the agreed spec (rather than just "tests pass now"), this looks like a reasonable, non-hacky implementation and I'd be fine approving.
